summary: Intermittent SSE disconnect behind AWS ALB strips 'end' event and duplicates trailing paragraph on resume
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that during intermittent network flaps through their ALB, SSE streams produced by our API sometimes arrive at the client missing the closing '</stream>' type end marker (we use a JSON control frame with event: "end"). Client reconnects, the resumed stream contains a duplicated trailing paragraph (the last sentence appears twice) and the response metadata envelope is repeated.

Impact: EditorFlow's editor integrations render partial HTML blobs and occasionally show duplicate concluding paragraphs. This leads to user confusion and corrupted saved drafts for a subset (~0.6%) of streaming sessions.

Environment: Production, routed through customer-managed AWS ALB that performs HTTP/2 fronting to our HTTP/1 edge. Customer uses server-sent events (SSE) streaming and a short client reconnect/backoff sequence.

Observed behavior: SSE stream terminates without emitting the standard '</stream>' type end marker (we use a JSON control frame with event: "end"). Client reconnect resumes with an earlier offset but the trailing paragraph is duplicated and trailing metadata block (conversation_id, timestamp) appears twice.

Expected behavior: On transient disconnects, stream resume should deliver a continuous output without duplicated sentences and should include a single, well-formed terminal control event indicating completion.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a long-running SSE generation request via the public API with chunked streaming enabled and a prompt that generates a 4+ paragraph response (example prompt attached).
2) Route traffic through an AWS ALB configured with HTTP/2 listener -> HTTP/1 target (same as customer config).
3) Induce a short connection flap by triggering an ALB target health probe during streaming (simulate by toggling backend target's socket for ~200-400ms).
4) Allow client to reconnect using normal resume logic (client sends last-received token index as resume_offset).
5) Observe the resumed stream: check for absence of 'end' control event and duplication of trailing paragraph and duplicate metadata envelope.
logs: edge-proxy (2026-03-10T15:12:03Z) INFO connection reset by peer: client socket closed during write, session_id=abc123
service-runtime (2026-03-10T15:12:03Z) WARN chunker: emitted-final-marker but upstream connection terminated before flush, request_id=rf-7f4c
edge-proxy (2026-03-10T15:12:04Z) INFO reconnect attempt from client ip 54.83.21.9, resume_offset=298
upstream (2026-03-10T15:12:04Z) INFO resumed session rf-7f4c at offset 298 and re-emitted buffered suffix length=72
client-side capture (EditorFlow) - final console: '...and that concludes our summary.' appears twice in sequence
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: ALB health probe / upgrade path may be causing partial TCP half-close that the edge-proxy interprets as a clean end, so the runtime flushes a final buffered suffix and then resume logic replays same suffix on reconnection.
Edge-proxy trace shows two metadata-envelope emits in quick succession during resume; need to determine whether duplication is from runtime replay or proxy retransmit logic.
Reproduced locally using a HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1 conversion proxy and a synthesized 300ms disconnect; observed missing 'end' control frame in 3/20 trials and duplicate trailing paragraph on 2/20 trials.

Binary tracing added: request_id rf-7f4c shows event sequence: CHUNK[n-1] -> CHUNK[n] (flushed) -> connection half-close -> client reconnect -> resume replay CHUNK[n] -> METADATA -> METADATA. The runtime's flush path writes CHUNK[n] and METADATA but does not mark session state as terminal when tcp half-close seen (race).

We suspect a race where the runtime's flush-on-half-close path emits the final chunk and metadata but fails to atomically set terminal flag; resume handler treats session as resumable and replays buffered suffix + metadata again.
comments: Support (2026-03-10): Thanks for the report — capturing details and routing to streaming infra. Can you attach a HAR or client capture? — Daniel
Customer (EditorFlow - 2026-03-10): Attached a client-side capture and ALB access log for two sample sessions. We see the repeated paragraph in both client and application logs.

SRE (2026-03-11): Reproduced on staging with an ALB-like proxy. Adding an internal tracepoint to the runtime to log terminal flag transitions (PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4281). — Liam O'Connor

Infra (2026-03-12): Patch to runtime replay logic created to add an atomic terminal set before flush returns success. Patch in review; test matrix shows duplicates eliminated in our harness. — Aisha Patel
root_cause: Race in runtime's flush-on-half-close path: final chunk and metadata could be emitted without atomically setting the session terminal flag. If a client reconnects quickly, resume handler replays buffered suffix and metadata producing duplicated trailing paragraph and duplicate metadata envelope.
workaround: Customer workaround: configure ALB idle timeout to be longer than typical keepalive (recommended 120s) and update client to use a brief exponential backoff (start at 200ms) before resuming to reduce resume/replay overlap. Also recommended: enable client-side de-duplication of immediate trailing sentences if present.
next_steps: 1) Merge runtime patch that sets terminal state atomically before flush (PR#4281).
2) Deploy patch to staging and run the ALB-proxy regression harness across 10k simulated stream sessions.
3) Coordinate a canary deploy to production for a subset of customers behind HTTP/2->HTTP/1 ALBs and monitor duplicate-trailer metric.
4) Follow up with EditorFlow to schedule a short maintenance window to test their ALB configuration and apply the recommended timeout change (if they accept).
5) Add a metric and alert for repeated metadata-envelope emits in a single session to catch regressions early.
resolution: In Progress - fix PR under review. Customer has applied the suggested ALB timeout and temporary client backoff; observed reduction in duplicates in their QA environment. Will update after production canary.
notes_for_postmortem: Consider adding a unit test that simulates TCP half-close during flush and asserts that terminal state is set before any resume unknowns.
Document guidance for customers using ALBs with HTTP/2 fronting and recommend default ALB idle timeout and client resume backoff settings in streaming best-practices page.
Instrument a lightweight 'resume-duplication' signal that increments when metadata envelope emitted more than once within 1s for same session_id.
